name: containerd
summary: A daemon and client architecture for managing container images, metadata, snapshots, tasks, and runtime shims through typed internal and external plugin boundaries.

features.name: Typed internal and external plugin boundaries
features.description: containerd defines plugin types for runtimes, snapshotters, content, metadata, services, and other subsystems. External plugins can be supplied as binaries or as local gRPC services without recompiling the daemon.
benefits: Allows subsystem implementations to evolve behind explicit interfaces
Permits deployment-time extension of a released daemon
costs: Plugin contracts and local IPC become compatibility and operational concerns
The system's behavior depends on configuration and the selected plugin set

features.name: Runtime v2 shim lifecycle
features.description: containerd selects a runtime for a container and invokes a runtime-v2 binary to start a shim; the shim then exposes the runtime shim API through which containerd starts and manages tasks.
benefits: Separates daemon lifetime from container task lifetime
Supports multiple runtime implementations selected per container
costs: Task, shim, and daemon lifecycles must remain coordinated
Runtime selection and shim discovery add configuration surface

features.name: Client-side high-level operations
features.description: The smart-client model leaves operations not required by the daemon, such as specification construction and registry interaction, in the client while the daemon provides shared lifecycle services.
benefits: Keeps the daemon focused on shared state and task management
Lets clients tailor image and container workflows
costs: Clients can differ in behavior and feature coverage
Some lifecycle intent is distributed across client and daemon boundaries

mathematical_views.question: How do daemon services, runtime implementations, snapshotters, and external endpoints compose into one container-management system?
assumptions: Plugin types are treated as typed vertices and configured dependencies as edges
The model abstracts transport and serialization details

mathematical_views.question: How does a container request move from runtime selection to an independently managed task?
assumptions: Runtime selection and shim startup are modeled as explicit transitions
The model does not assert that every transition succeeds
The shim API abstracts individual task implementation details

costs: More interfaces, configuration, and IPC failure modes

benefits: Runtime-specific task management with daemon isolation
A smaller shared daemon and flexible clients
